a2-b114: With MDMA, I treat meaningful jaw tension as the earliest warning that the body needs more magnesium. Nobody has tested this in a trial that I know of, so it's from what I've seen again and again: everyone I know who took enough magnesium chloride for the jaw tension to fully release avoided the other complications I've seen in people who let the tension keep going.
a2-b115: A token dose may not be enough to make the jaw release. More than once, I've dissolved Dead Sea magnesium chloride hexahydrate flakes in water and taken about one gram per minute by mouth for around twenty minutes before mine fully released. I can take around twenty grams without diarrhea, which for me only starts above about forty grams. Magnesium chloride is also less likely to cause diarrhea than several other kinds of magnesium, including the ones people take on purpose as laxatives.
a2-b117p:
Magnesium taken before the MDMA peak also makes the peak less euphoric for me, but I'll take slightly less euphoria for a relaxed jaw, since in my experience the risk of the night turning into an emergency is much lower then.

What happened to my second wife is why I look past magnesium: she had severe convulsions after an MDMA overdose, and at the hospital they found her potassium critically low, described to me as essentially zero. IV potassium was the only treatment they gave her. So I treat serious MDMA toxicity as a broader electrolyte emergency, potassium included, even though magnesium is still the first and most useful intervention once the jaw tenses.

a2-b120: If someone has impaired kidneys, they do need to be more cautious with large and rapid magnesium doses, because they may not clear magnesium normally. The MDMA is a far bigger danger to their kidneys, though. Besides overheating them and causing dangerous electrolyte shifts, it can hurt the kidneys directly. Acute kidney injury can come from the MDMA itself or from the muscle breakdown it brings on (rhabdomyolysis). So kidney trouble is a strong reason to skip the drug altogether, and once someone with it has taken some, their jaw tension still needs treating. With serious kidney impairment, I wouldn't have them copy my one-gram-per-minute approach as is. I'd treat their case as higher-risk and call medics sooner than I would for someone with healthy kidneys.
